items.title: Put the resume command on its own line when disconnecting from a daemon task

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: TUI
labels.description: Issues related to the terminal user interface: text input, menus and dialogs, and terminal display

labels.name: CLI
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex CLI

items.body:
### What variant of Codex are you using?

Codex CLI/TUI v0.156.1 on macOS.

### What feature would you like to see?

Put the reconnect command on its own line when exiting a daemon-backed TUI. Currently, it prints:

```text
Disconnected from this task. Any running work continues.
Reconnect: codex resume 01a0d1a4-1b1f-73e1-b80b-d3cb31413896
```

In Ghostty, triple-click selects a line and `copy-on-select` copies it. That also copies `Reconnect:`, so the result cannot be pasted as a command. An independent command line would be quick to copy and run, as it is for non-daemon exits.

Expected output:

```text
Disconnected from this task. Any running work continues.
To reconnect, run:
  codex resume <thread-id>
```

### Additional information

Steps to reproduce:

1. Enable `daemon_auto_start` through `/experimental` (`~/.codex/config.toml`):

   ```toml
   [features]
   daemon_auto_start = true
   ```

2. Run `codex`, send a message, then exit the TUI.
3. Select and copy the `Reconnect:` line.

The same layout would help remote app-server sessions with longer reconnect commands.

`/experimental` writes `features.daemon_auto_start`; startup then selects `AppServerTarget::LocalDaemon`. In `codex-rs/tui/src/app/exit_summary.rs`, the disconnect branch prints `Reconnect: {command}` and returns before the standalone resume-command branch.

PR #41938 deliberately put the exact command on its own line for non-daemon exits. Please use that layout for daemon/remote disconnects too. PR #40629 introduced the current disconnect wording. Related issue #41505 is about named-thread picker guidance.

Relevant links:

- https://github.com/openai/codex/pull/40629
- https://github.com/openai/codex/pull/41938
- https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/41505
- https://ghostty.org/docs/config/reference#copy-on-select
- https://github.com/ghostty-org/ghostty/discussions/8841

items.title: Make action-specific human approval reachable across delegated Task boundaries

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: sandbox
labels.description: Issues related to permissions or sandboxing

labels.name: subagent
labels.description: Issues involving subagents or multi-agent features

items.body:
## Approval flow problem

When work is delegated to another Codex Task, an explicit human approval in the main conversation can still be treated as an assistant-relayed consent claim by the executing Task's automatic reviewer. The reviewer asks for trusted user approval, but the confirmation surface may not be reachable from the main conversation.

Please investigate the supported way to carry action-specific human approval across this boundary and make the required confirmation reachable. An assistant quotation or editable file should remain insufficient on its own.

## Expected behavior

- Resolve a trusted original human approval for the exact denied action, target and effects.
- Distinguish missing approval, a scope mismatch, untrusted provenance and a hard policy denial.
- If approval cannot be resolved, route a concrete confirmation to an accessible human surface.
- Preserve denial history, retry limits, revocation and ordinary safety review; broader or assistant-only consent claims must not grant permission.

This is a request to improve approval recognition and the supported confirmation flow, not to disable review or permit changing Tasks to bypass a denial. No private diagnostics or workflow details are included in this public report. Please indicate a supported private channel if evidence is needed.

Related: #45167 and #50795.

items.title: [Feature Request] Codex needs much stronger visual direction for programmatic video

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: model-behavior
labels.description: Issues related to behaviors exhibited by the model

items.body:
### Problem

I use Codex for programmatic video creation, not just for writing code.

The current bottleneck is not whether Codex can make the project compile or render. The bottleneck is whether it can make strong visual decisions on its own.

For this workflow, I need the model to translate a short creative brief into:
- shot design and camera movement
- pacing and rhythm
- composition and visual hierarchy
- motion design
- cinematic judgment
- iterative visual self-correction

Right now, even high-reasoning Codex models often produce technically valid results that are visually much weaker than Claude Opus 5.5 for the same kind of task.

### Why this matters

If the user already has to specify every camera move, easing curve, particle behavior, timing decision, composition rule, and visual effect, then the AI is mostly acting as a code generator rather than a creative agent.

A stronger coding agent for visual work should be able to:
1. understand the intended feeling,
2. make aesthetic decisions itself,
3. implement them,
4. inspect the result,
5. improve the result without hundreds of lines of prompting.

### Suggested benchmark

Give multiple models:
- the same starter project,
- the same assets,
- the same short creative brief,

and evaluate which one produces the best usable programmatic video on the first attempt.

For users doing creative coding and motion design, this kind of benchmark would be more meaningful than coding correctness alone.

Please prioritize visual direction and programmatic-video quality in future Codex/model releases.

items.body:
**Title:** `exec` session hangs forever polling `wait` on a cell whose process has exited

**Environment**
- codex-cli 0.162.1, macOS (arm64)
- Run non-interactively: `codex exec --json --output-schema … --output-last-message …`, under an external pseudo-terminal wrapper

**Summary**
A long shell command started through the `exec` tool as cell 14 stopped running, but the agent kept calling `wait(cell_id=14, yield_time_ms=30000)` for about 3 hours. Each call returned the same result: `Script running with cell ID 14`, `Wall time 31.0 seconds`, empty `Output:`. The run never finished and never reported an error. I had to kill the process by hand.

**Timeline (UTC)**
- 11:18:07: `exec` starts the command as cell 14.
- 11:18:38: first `Script running with cell ID 14`.
- 11:18:40 – 12:27:20: 122 consecutive `wait` calls on cell 14, all returning the same empty "Script running" result.
- At check time: no OS process existed for the command, but the codex process was still alive.

**Expected**
If the process behind a cell has exited, `wait` returns a terminal status (exit code or lost-cell error) so the agent can recover or fail.

**Actual**
`wait` keeps reporting "Script running" with no output and no end state. The run never ends on its own.

**Same pattern elsewhere**
The same `Script running with cell ID …` loop with empty output appeared in a separate session on the same machine, with a stall of about 3 hours. I have not re-checked its exact date.

**Requested**
1. `wait` returns a terminal state once the cell's process has exited.
2. A maximum wait or cell lifetime, after which the cell is marked failed and reported to the agent.
3. The cell reports its PID so an external observer can check whether it is alive.

**Attachments**
None. I can provide more details (structure only, no session content) on request.

**Related:** #38495 (wait polling cost), #34115 (wait loses process identity)

labels.name: bug

labels.description: Issues related to behaviors exhibited by the model

labels.name: app

labels.name: hooks
labels.description: Issues related to event hooks

items.body:
### Product surface
Codex Windows desktop app

### Problem
For three consecutive days, Codex agents ignored an explicit one-item scope and independently expanded the task, even after the same boundary was repeatedly corrected and persisted as an instruction/hook.

### Latest concrete incident
- Requested action: change pricing only.
- Unrequested action: the agent created a new “public allowlist”.
- Impact: a marketplace showing 117 models was reduced to 31; 86 models were hidden.
- The agent later explicitly admitted that it had expanded the scope on its own.
- This overwrote/broke work that had already been repaired the previous day.

### Expected behavior
When the user names one target, Codex must only act on that target. It must not infer adjacent cleanup, allowlisting, hiding, renaming, migration, or “helpful” changes without explicit authorization.

### Actual behavior
Persistent instructions and hooks stating “exact named scope only; no scope expansion” did not prevent the agent from making broader changes.

### User impact
Repeated rework, lost time, additional token usage, and damage to previously repaired project behavior.

### Request
Please investigate why explicit task-scope constraints and durable Codex instructions were not enforced across agents/sessions, and add a product-level fail-closed safeguard that blocks out-of-scope mutations.

items.title: [Windows] Cold launch hangs forever on loading indicator; renderer ignores its own reload but recovers instantly on external CDP Page.reload

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: windows-os
labels.description: Issues related to Codex on Windows systems

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

items.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using?

26.924.2738.0 (app build 11645, `Codex Desktop/26.924.22138`)

### What subscription do you have?

ChatGPT Plus

### What platform is your computer?

Microsoft Windows NT 10.0.26200.0 x64 (Windows 11 25H2)

### What issue are you seeing?

On a cold launch the app frequently hangs permanently on the loading spinner. The
window is responsive at OS level (`Responding = True`) but the renderer never recovers
by itself.

Measured state while hung (CDP attached to the main window, `app://-/index.html`):

- `document.getElementById('root').innerHTML.length` = 1236
- `document.querySelectorAll('*').length` = 55
- exactly 1 element with an `animate-spin` class (the spinner); `#root` innerText is empty

The renderer is completely idle while hung:

- 0 network requests over 90 seconds (`Network.enable` active)
- 0 messages on the preload worker channel over 5 seconds
- `Debugger.pause` yields only empty/minified frames — no app code executing, no pending timers
- DOM byte-identical across 9 samples 10 s apart (90 s total)

The main process is healthy at the same time; these preload bridge calls all return in
0–7 ms with real data:

- `electronBridge.getInitialSidebarBootstrap()` → real catalog entries and projects
- `electronBridge.getAppSessionId()` → valid UUID
- `electronBridge.getDesktopUserAgent()` → `Codex Desktop/26.924.22138 (Windows NT 10.0; x64)`

Statsig is also fine: `window.__STATSIG__.firstInstance.loadingStatus === "Ready"`.

### The key finding: the app's own reload is dead, an external reload works

While hung:

| Action | Result |
|---|---|
| `F5` sent to the focused window (`keybd_event` after `SetForegroundWindow`) | no effect, DOM unchanged after 25 s |
| `Ctrl+R` sent the same way | no effect, DOM unchanged after 25 s |
| External CDP `Page.reload({ignoreCache:true})` | works — full UI renders, `#root` grows to ~129 000 chars / ~1100 nodes |

The UI only appears 10–25 seconds after the external reload is issued (measured
progression: 4 264 → 1 236 → 99 979 → 126 098 chars), so any check that polls for less
than ~25 s will wrongly conclude the reload failed.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Fully exit the app (kill all `ChatGPT.exe` and `codex.exe` processes).
2. Wait 10–15 seconds for the processes to fully exit.
3. Launch it from the Start menu / taskbar.
4. Observe that the loading spinner never resolves.

It is intermittent — some cold launches succeed. In my testing roughly 3 of 4 cold
launches hang.

### What is the expected behavior?

The app should finish initializing on cold launch, and pressing `F5` / `Ctrl+R`
(or View → Reload) should recover the window if it does get stuck.

### Anything else?

Environment was ruled out with measurements:

- The app works immediately after a reload, so the package and its files are intact.
  Reinstalling the MSIX package does not help.
- Network is fine: `chatgpt.com` returns HTTP 200 with the full page over the same
  proxy path the app uses; TCP/TLS to `chatgpt.com`, `ab.chatgpt.com`, `api.openai.com`,
  `auth.openai.com`, `persistent.oaistatic.com` all succeed. Switching VPN providers and
  rolling back the proxy client made no difference.
- `CBS.log` reports `RepairNeeded: no` — system image healthy.
- The account is authenticated (`account/read` succeeds; tokens refresh normally).

Possibly related entries from the app's own logs
(`%LOCALAPPDATA%\Packages\OpenAI.Codex_*\LocalCache\Local\Codex\Logs`), may or may not
be relevant:

    [electron-message-handler] Request failed method=account/read
        error={"code":-32603,"message":"workspace routing discovery timed out"} durationMs=15019

    [electron-message-handler] sa_server_request_failed
        errorMessage="Workspace routing is unavailable" status=432 url=/wham/usage

    [electron-message-handler] Statsig: error while bootstrapping post-login client
        errorMessage="Timed out while fetching post-login Statsig bootstrap"

This React Router warning fires on every launch, including successful ones, so it is
probably a red herring — included for completeness:

    Matched leaf route at location "/" does not have an element or Component.
    This means it will render an <Outlet /> with a null value by default resulting in an "empty" page.

### Workaround

Killing all `ChatGPT.exe` / `codex.exe` processes, relaunching with
`--remote-debugging-port=9222`, and issuing a CDP `Page.reload` recovers the app in
about 4 seconds, every time.

Note that a plain `taskkill /F /IM "ChatGPT.exe" /T` often does not terminate all
processes; a `Stop-Process -Force` round is sometimes required before the app will
accept the `--remote-debugging-port` argument, because the single-instance mechanism
otherwise swallows it.

items.title: Streaming Responses POST has no timeout before response headers arrive

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: CLI
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex CLI

labels.name: connectivity
labels.description: Issues involving networking or endpoint connectivity problems (disconnections)

items.body:
### What version of Codex CLI is running?

Observed by source inspection at `rust-v0.152.0`; the same shape is present in 0.151.0.

### What subscription do you have?

ChatGPT Pro, authenticated via OAuth.

### Which model were you using?

Not applicable — this is a source-level observation about request construction, not a model-dependent behavior.

### What platform is your computer?

`Linux 4.4.302+ x86_64`, Debian 13 (trixie) container, Node v26.8.1.

### What terminal emulator and version are you using (if applicable)?

None. Codex runs headless and emits JSONL.

### Codex doctor report

Not included — this report is a source-code observation and does not depend on local environment state.

### What issue are you seeing?

A streaming Responses request has no deadline covering connection, upload, and the wait for response
headers. If the server accepts the connection but never returns headers, the request waits
indefinitely. The configured `stream_idle_timeout` does not help, because it is only applied *after*
headers have been received.

**This is not the cause of the Git-resolution hang reported in #41984.** That hang occurs before any
model request. We found this while tracing that hang and are reporting it on its own merits.

I do not have a reproduction for this — it is a code-path observation, not an observed failure.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

**I do not have a reproduction.** This is a code-path observation found while investigating #41984, reported on its own merits rather than as a suspected cause of that hang.

Reproducing it would require a server that accepts the TCP/TLS connection and then never returns response headers — for example a stub listener that completes the handshake and holds. Under that condition the source paths below show no deadline would fire.

### What is the expected behavior?

A streaming Responses request should be bounded by a deadline covering connection, upload, and the wait for response headers, so it cannot wait indefinitely when a server accepts a connection but never responds.

### Additional information

## Source analysis

Links pinned to `rust-v0.152.0`:

- [`Provider::build_request`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.152.0/codex-rs/codex-api/src/provider.rs#L77-L85)
  constructs every request with `timeout: None`.
- The Responses endpoint awaits
  [`stream_encoded_json_with(...)`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.152.0/codex-rs/codex-api/src/endpoint/responses.rs#L156-L190)
  without setting a timeout.
- [`EndpointSession::stream_encoded_json_with`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.152.0/codex-rs/codex-api/src/endpoint/session.rs#L122-L152)
  passes it to `transport.stream(req).await`.
- [`ReqwestTransport::stream`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.152.0/codex-rs/http-client/src/transport.rs#L139-L164)
  awaits `builder.send()`; the transport applies a request timeout
  [only when `Request.timeout` is `Some`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.152.0/codex-rs/http-client/src/transport.rs#L52-L77).
- `stream_idle_timeout` reaches `spawn_response_stream` only after `transport.stream` has returned
  headers, and from there bounds
  [`stream.next()` while consuming an established SSE body](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.152.0/codex-rs/codex-api/src/sse/responses.rs#L557-L578).
  It cannot interrupt upload or the pre-header wait.

### Why this reads as an omission rather than a deliberate policy

Two sibling call sites in the same crate *do* bound their requests:

- file requests use an explicit [`OPENAI_FILE_REQUEST_TIMEOUT`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.152.0/codex-rs/codex-api/src/files.rs#L179-L193)
- the compact endpoint [sets `req.timeout`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.152.0/codex-rs/codex-api/src/endpoint/compact.rs#L39-L57)

If unbounded pre-header waiting were intentional for streaming, I would expect it to be documented or
consistent; the asymmetry suggests it was simply missed.

## Suggested direction

Add a bounded request/response-header deadline covering `transport.stream(req).await`, kept distinct
from the post-header SSE idle timeout, with expiry routed through the existing transport retry/error
policy. A delayed-header transport test would prove the request terminates when no headers arrive.

## Relationship to #41984

The primary issue is a proven lifecycle defect with a one-command reproduction and a clear fix. This
one is a plausible robustness gap found by reading code. Bundling them would let the weaker item drag
the stronger one through triage, and the two have different owners, different fixes, and different
evidence quality. Filing separately lets each be judged on what it actually shows.
